children: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (NSE:BPCL) posted strong Q2 operationals—₹90bn EBITDA, ₹4,993cr profit, 117% refinery runs and $32.5/bbl margin—while shifting supply toward the Middle East, buying 37% Russian crude, facing LPG under-recoveries and policy duty changes that may pressure near-term earnings.
: BPCL Q2: standalone EBITDA ₹90bn, profit ₹4,993cr, refinery run 117%, sales 14.06 MMT, refining margin $32.5/bbl, capex ₹1.7 lakh crore for refinery, gas, petrochemicals, green energy
Diesel Export Duty Hike, Petrol Exemption
: Govt raised diesel export duty to Rs 11.5/litre and cut petrol export duty to zero for the fortnight from Oct 31; changes directly affect state oil firms including Bharat Petroleum (BPCL).
: BPCL said Russian oil accounted for about 37% of its crude purchases in the July–September quarter, specifying Russia’s share of its total crude sourcing for that period.
: BPCL reported LPG under-recoveries of ₹17,334.40 crore through September. Industry LPG under-recoveries reached ₹67,900 crore. Delayed government subsidies noted; under-recoveries likely to rise.
: BPCL reported higher crude and product supplies from the Middle East this quarter versus Q1 and expects further Middle Eastern sourcing in October–November, citing a shift in its supply mix.
: BPCL says premium for December Russian crude fell to about $1–$2/ bbl from roughly $12–$13/ bbl in October, narrowing the price gap for those cargoes.
: Nomura kept a Buy on Bharat Petroleum (BPCL) and cut its target to Rs 385 from Rs 395, citing high crude oil prices that may pressure near-term earnings and Q3 FY27 results.
: BPCL tendered for ethanol supplies from November, pricing maize-based ethanol at Rs 68.86/l and cutting incentive to Rs 2.79/l, reflecting feedstock cost shifts and grain-based sourcing.
